title: Juicy Peruvian Beans Talavera-Plate Tacu Tacu
description: A comforting and citrusy Peruvian dish featuring shortening, bain-marie, and a macrobiotic-friendly twist, served in a beautiful Talavera plate with a delicious cheese pull.

ingredients.name: kidney beans
ingredients.notes: canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: shortening
ingredients.notes: vegetable shortening, like coconut oil or avocado oil

instructions: Heat the shortening in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then saut99 the chopped onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for another minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the kidney beans, oregano, cumin, and lemon juice, mixing well to combine.
Transfer the mixture to a bain-marie, a double boiler setup, and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, prepare the cheese topping by crumbling the melted cheese into small pieces.
Once the bean mixture is ready, carefully transfer it to a Talavera plate, creating a shallow well in the center.
Spoon the cheese topping into the well, and place the plate under the broiler until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove the plate from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving, garnished with additional orange zest if desired.
Serve warm, and enjoy the comforting and citrusy flavors of this Peruvian dish!
Garnish with additional orange zest if desired, for a vibrant and colorful presentation.
Serve with a side of steamed vegetables or a green salad for a well-rounded meal.
For an extra touch, add a sprinkle of chopped fresh cilantro or scallions on top of the cheese topping.
